author: Alex Carter - Sports Editor
title: Rybakina Beats Osaka in Three-Set Thriller to Reach Canadian Open Semi-Finals
text:
During the intense summer hard-court swing leading up to the US Open, Elena Rybakina engineered a gritty three-set comeback victory against Naomi Osaka, winning 4-6, 7-6 (7-5), 6-4 in a two-hour and 33-minute quarter-final clash at the Canadian Open in Toronto, according to tournament reporting from the BBC.
Tactical Breakdown of the Toronto Quarter-Final Osaka seized the early momentum on court, breaking Rybakina in the opening game to capture the first set. The four-time major winner extended her control into the second frame, building a 4-2 advantage despite dropping serve once. However, the 2022 Wimbledon and 2026 Australian Open champion mounted a severe counter-offensive. Rybakina reeled off three consecutive games, clinched the ensuing tie-break to level the match, and ultimately weathered four missed break points by Osaka at 3-2 in the deciding set before securing the break that paved the way to victory.
According to match accounts, Rybakina accumulated 72 unforced errors—her highest single-match tally of the current season—yet offset the misfires with sheer power, sealing the contest with her 15th ace of the evening. Reflecting on the physical and mental toll of the encounter, Rybakina stated to broadcasters, “I was just trying to fight. The first game was really tough because it cost me the set, and then in the second I was just trying to stay closer to the score, even if I’m losing. I’m super happy that I won this match.”
Draw Implications and Subsequent Withdrawals Rybakina advances directly to the semi-finals to face Coco Gauff, who progressed after Belinda Bencic withdrew from their match due to a hip injury, as detailed by the BBC. On the opposite side of the bracket, Iga Swiatek secured a commanding 6-2, 6-1 victory against Diana Shnaider, setting up a final-four showdown against Elina Svitolina, who defeated Ekaterina Alexandrova 3-6, 6-0, 6-3.
Photo: bbc.com Meanwhile, the physical demands of the tour continue to reshape player schedules ahead of the final major of the year. Following her quarter-final exit, Osaka announced her withdrawal from the upcoming Cincinnati Open—traditionally the final major tune-up before the US Open—citing fatigue.
